findings.evidence: The roadmap at lines 970–974 explicitly requires finite-index data for `V ≤ U` and `U ≤ G`; the new relative maps already use `[(V.subgroupOf U).FiniteIndex]`, but all three transitivity theorem signatures instead require `[U.FiniteIndex] [V.FiniteIndex]`.
findings.fix: Replace `[V.FiniteIndex]` with `[(V.subgroupOf U).FiniteIndex]` in all three laws and derive the finite index of V in G internally from the relative and outer instances.
findings.issue: `explicitCor0_trans`, `explicitCor1_trans` (line 333), and `explicitCor2_trans` (line 362) assume `[V.FiniteIndex]`, whereas transitivity is specified with finite-index data for `V ≤ U` and `U ≤ G`.

summary: The transitivity laws require finite index of V directly in G instead of the promised relative finite-index data for V ≤ U, so the formal statements do not expose the roadmap’s intended hypothesis.
